text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The government may substitute some under-secretaries of state in February 1997, government sources told the paper.
- The state will assume the management of 300 billion escudos of liabilities of state railway company CP-Caminhos de Ferro Portugueses.
- The coordinator in the partial privatisation of electricity company EDP will be announced in January, under-secretary of state for finance, Fernando Teixeira dos Santos, told the paper.
- Delays in the Socialist government's decision about constitutional revision and regionalisation is irritating members of parliament.
- Electricity company EDP is in talks to buy a 20 percent stake in mobile phone operator Telecel from Telepri and Air Touch for about 34 billion escudos, the newspaper learned.
- Parliament passed the 1997 budget, with abstentions by the Social Democratic Party (PSD) and the small rightwing Popular Party (PP). The Communist Party (PCP) voted against the budget.
- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres asked Culture Minister Manuel Maria Carrilho to change a decree which forgives the debts of film producers to the state after five years.
- Popular Party (PP) leader Manuel Monteiro will only decide tomorrow whether to run for the PP leadership at a weekend congress, the paper said.

- Under-secretary for European Matters Seixas da Costa is optimistic about the EU Dublin summit which starts today. In an interview with the paper, Seixas da Costa says he expects concrete measures in preparation for the EU single currency to be adopted.
